page: Microsoft Azure FX12-6mds_v2 is a constrained-vCPU instance within the compute-optimized and memory-intensive FXmdsv2 family, provisioned on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 6 vCPUs derived from 3 dedicated physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at a base clock frequency of 4.2 GHz. Supported by 260 MB of L3 cache, the underlying x86_64 architecture incorporates modern instruction sets, including AVX-512, Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for int8 and tile matrix operations, and hardware cryptography acceleration via VAES and SHA-NI.

Despite being grouped in a compute-oriented family, the configuration provides an exceptionally high memory allocation of 252.0 GB of RAM, equating to 42.0 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture includes a bundled 944 GB local NVMe SSD alongside compatibility with Azure Premium Storage volumes. The configuration does not include a dedicated GPU accelerator, relying entirely on the host CPU for compute tasks.

Performance benchmarks reflect the high 4.2 GHz CPU clock speed, yielding a Geekbench single-core score of 2357.0 (top 10%) and top-tier text processing metrics (2951.0). Single-threaded data handling tests show strong results, including 34.96 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.44 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. However, due to the constrained 6-vCPU allocation, aggregate multi-threaded compute remains in the mid-tier category, as shown by a PassMark CPU score of 12021.43 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 7305.0. CPU-bound large language model inference drops significantly on models larger than 7B parameters.

This instance profile delivers high cost efficiency for software licenses billed on a per-core basis that simultaneously demand massive in-memory capacities and high per-thread execution speed. Primary workload fits include in-memory databases such as Redis, relational database engines with high cache requirements, electronic design automation (EDA), financial modeling, and batch compression tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure FX12-6mds_v2 is a specialized instance designed for workloads demanding high per-core execution speeds paired with extensive memory capacity. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz, the instance delivers 6 dedicated vCPUs (3 physical cores), 260 MB of L3 cache, and 252.0 GB of RAM, resulting in an exceptional 42.0 GB of memory per core. The host includes a 944 GB local NVMe SSD for high-speed scratch storage and omits dedicated GPUs. In benchmark evaluations, the server achieves top-tier single-threaded performance, scoring 2357.0 in Geekbench single-core and 34.96 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression, while multi-core metrics remain moderate due to the 6-vCPU topology. This architecture provides cost efficiency for core-licensed environments requiring high single-thread throughput and expansive RAM, such as in-memory databases, electronic design automation, financial analytics, and memory-heavy transactional processing.
